_about: WATCH (32) instruction cards from 'Astronaut Acute Health Decision Tree, v3'. The package goes with the next planned communication. Follow-up times are proposals. If a new symptom appears the tree can always be reopened.

C-BURN-MINOR.title: Minor burn
now: Cool for 20 minutes. Microgravity: wet cloth or cold pack. Landing-surface: cool water or wet cloth.
If it has blistered, do not burst it.
Apply burn cream and a non-stick dressing.
C-BURN-MINOR.followUp: After 24 hours, then once a day for 3 days: "Has redness or discharge increased? Is there fever?" Yes → C-SKIN-INFECTION.

C-HEAD-MINOR.title: Minor blow to the head
now: Apply cold to the place of the blow.
C-HEAD-MINOR.then: A crewmate keeps watch for 24 hours.
C-HEAD-MINOR.followUp: After 2, 6 and 24 hours: "Is there vomiting, worsening headache or confusion?" Yes → C-HEAD-SEVERE.

C-CUT-MINOR.title: Minor cut / scrape
now: Rinse with clean water (Microgravity: with an absorbent pad); apply antiseptic.
Cover with a plaster.
C-CUT-MINOR.followUp: After 24 hours, then once a day: "Is redness or swelling spreading?" Yes → C-SKIN-INFECTION.

C-STRAIN.title: Muscle / joint strain
now: Rest the area; stop the exercise that hurts.
Apply cold for 20 minutes.
C-STRAIN.then: Repeat cold for the first 48 hours; support with an elastic bandage; use a simple painkiller if needed.
C-STRAIN.followUp: After 48 and 72 hours: "Has the pain eased? Is there pain at one point on the bone?" Not eased or one-point pain → C-FRACTURE-SUSPECTED.

C-LENS.title: Contact-lens related eye irritation
now: Remove the lens at once.
Rinse with artificial tears.
C-LENS.followUp: After 24 hours: "Is redness or stinging still there? Has vision decreased?" Still there → antibiotic drops (per kit procedure); vision decreased → A-EYE.

C-EYE-FOREIGN-BODY.title: Particle in the eye
now: Do not rub the eye.
Rinse with the eyewash kit (Microgravity: with the closed cap).
C-EYE-FOREIGN-BODY.followUp: After 24 hours: "Has the stinging gone?" No → C-EYE-GENERAL.

C-EYE-IRRITATION.title: Eye irritation
now: Use artificial tears.
Take a break from the screen.
C-EYE-IRRITATION.then: Check cabin humidity and air flow.
C-EYE-IRRITATION.followUp: After 24 hours: "Has the irritation gone?" No → C-EYE-GENERAL.

C-EYE-GENERAL.title: Unclear eye complaint
now: Test and record the vision of both eyes.
C-EYE-GENERAL.followUp: Repeat the vision test after 24 hours: "Did the result change?" One line lost → C-SANS; sudden loss → A-EYE.

C-TOOTH-FRACTURE.title: Broken tooth / lost filling
now: Rinse the mouth with clean water.
Apply the temporary filling from the dental kit (needs training).
C-TOOTH-FRACTURE.followUp: After 24 hours: "Is there pain or swelling?" Yes → dental branch (DS1).

C-TOOTH-PAIN.title: Toothache
now: Rinse the mouth with warm water; use dental floss.
Use a simple painkiller if needed.
C-TOOTH-PAIN.followUp: After 24 hours: "Is there swelling or fever?" Yes → dental branch (DS1).

C-BREATHING.title: Upper respiratory tract infection
now: Rest, drink plenty of fluids.
Take care with hand hygiene; wear a mask.
C-BREATHING.followUp: Temperature is read automatically twice a day; every 12 hours: "Is there shortness of breath?" Shortness of breath or fever longer than 3 days → C-BREATHING-SEVERE.

C-ALLERGY-MILD.title: Mild allergic reaction
now: Stop the suspected trigger and note it.
Allergy medication: per kit procedure.
C-ALLERGY-MILD.followUp: After 1, 2 and 4 hours: "Is there swelling of lips or tongue, or shortness of breath?" Yes → A-ANAPHYLAXIS at once.

C-CONGESTION.title: Head and face fullness (fluid shift to the head)
now: Use the decongestant spray for a short time.
C-CONGESTION.then: Check cabin humidity and CO₂. Exercise helps fluid distribution.
C-CONGESTION.followUp: After 24 hours: "Has vision blurred?" Yes → C-SANS.

C-CO2.title: Carbon-dioxide related headache (one person)
now: Move to a well-ventilated area.
Check the cabin CO₂ value (the panel records it).
C-CO2.then: Drink fluids, take a break; use a simple painkiller if needed; check the CO₂ removal system per procedure.
C-CO2.followUp: After 1 hour: "Has the headache gone?" If it starts in someone else too → environment rule; nausea, confusion or fast breathing → A-ENVIRONMENT.

C-HEADACHE.title: Headache
now: Drink fluids, rest.
Use a simple painkiller if needed.
C-HEADACHE.then: Record the severity (1–10) and duration of the pain.
C-HEADACHE.followUp: After 4 hours: "Did the pain become sudden and very severe? Is speech affected?" Yes → A-BRAIN.

C-DERMATITIS.title: Skin rash / dryness
now: Clean and dry the area.
Apply moisturiser or the cream from the kit.
C-DERMATITIS.then: Check for rubbing clothing or a sensor strap; take a photo.
C-DERMATITIS.followUp: After 48 hours: "Is the rash spreading, hot or swollen?" Yes → C-SKIN-INFECTION.

C-UTI.title: Suspected urinary tract infection
now: Drink plenty of fluids.
If a urine test strip is available, test.
C-UTI.followUp: After 12 hours: "Has fever or flank pain started?" Yes → C-UTI-SEVERE.

C-CONSTIPATION.title: Constipation
now: Take fluids and fibre-rich food.
Stool softener: per kit procedure.
C-CONSTIPATION.followUp: After 24 hours: "Is there vomiting, or is no gas passing?" Yes → A-ABDOMEN.

C-ADAPTATION.title: Space adaptation syndrome (motion sickness)
now: Keep the head still; avoid sudden movement.
Anti-nausea medication: per kit procedure.
C-ADAPTATION.then: If vomiting, replace lost fluids. It usually passes in a few days.
C-ADAPTATION.followUp: Once a day for 3 days: "Is vomiting continuing? Can you take fluids?" If fluids cannot be taken, the package goes in the first communication window.

C-ABDOMEN-GENERAL.title: Abdominal discomfort
now: Eat light food, drink fluids.
Measure temperature.
C-ABDOMEN-GENERAL.followUp: After 4–6 hours: "Has the pain settled at one point? Is there fever or vomiting?" Settled in the lower right → C-APPENDICITIS; other yes answers → abdominal branch (K1) again.

C-BACK.title: Space-related low back pain
now: Rest with the knees pulled to the chest.
Use a simple painkiller if needed.
C-BACK.followUp: After 72 hours: "Is there pain or numbness spreading to the leg?" Yes → C-NERVE.

C-NERVE.title: Suspected pinched nerve
now: Avoid movements that hurt.
Use a simple painkiller if needed.
C-NERVE.followUp: Once a day: "Has arm or leg strength decreased? Is bladder or bowel control affected?" Yes → the package goes at EMERGENCY priority.

C-MUSCLE-GENERAL.title: Musculoskeletal pain
now: Rest it; apply warmth or cold.
C-MUSCLE-GENERAL.followUp: After 72 hours: "Has the pain eased?" No → musculoskeletal branch (KS1) again.

C-EVA-HAND.title: Hand / nail problem from the EVA glove
now: Photograph the hands and nails.
Do not pull off a lifted nail; protect it with tape.
C-EVA-HAND.followUp: After 4 hours: "Has the numbness eased? Is there joint pain or weakness?" Numbness spread, joint pain or weakness started → A-DCS.

C-FEVER.title: Illness with fever
now: Measure temperature, drink fluids, rest.
Fever reducer: per kit procedure.
C-FEVER.then: Look for the source: cough, urine, wound, tooth.
C-FEVER.followUp: Temperature is read automatically every 4 hours and qSOFA is calculated; every 4 hours: "Is there confusion or fast breathing?" Yes or qSOFA ≥2 → A-SEPSIS.

C-PALPITATIONS.title: Palpitations
now: Secure yourself; breathe slowly and deeply.
Take an ECG recording.
C-PALPITATIONS.then: Note triggers such as caffeine, lack of sleep, stress.
C-PALPITATIONS.followUp: ECG is monitored continuously; ECG red → A-RHYTHM automatically. After 24 hours: "Was there chest pain or a feeling of fainting?" Yes → A-HEART or A-RHYTHM.

C-FATIGUE.title: General weakness
now: Measure pulse, SpO₂, temperature and blood pressure.
C-FATIGUE.then: Sort out fluids, nutrition and sleep; lighten the workload.
C-FATIGUE.followUp: After 24 hours: "Has it got worse?" Yes, or any reading yellow → the tree is reopened from the start.

C-PANIC.title: Panic / anxiety attack
now: Move to a calm area; a crewmate stays with you.
Breathe in for 4 seconds, hold for 4, breathe out over 6.
C-PANIC.then: Take an ECG recording to make sure it is not from the heart.
C-PANIC.followUp: After 24 hours: "Did the attack happen again?" On the third attack → C-STRESS and a request for psychological support in the first communication.

C-SLEEP.title: Sleep disturbance
now: Fix your sleep hours.
Reduce light and noise in the sleep area.
C-SLEEP.then: No caffeine in the afternoon. Sleep medication: per kit procedure.
C-SLEEP.followUp: Actigraphy records sleep duration automatically for 7 days. If the 7-day average is below 6 hours, the red gate opens on the mission readiness card and the package goes in the first window.

C-LOW-MOOD.title: Low mood / depressive mood
now: Keep the daily routine and exercise.
Spend time with crewmates.
C-LOW-MOOD.then: Ask for a psychological support session in the first communication.
C-LOW-MOOD.followUp: On day 3 and day 7: "Are there thoughts of self-harm?" Yes → A-PSYCH at once.

C-STRESS.title: Stress
now: Review the workload with the crew lead.
Set aside time for rest and exercise.
C-STRESS.then: If you wish, ask for a psychological support session.
C-STRESS.followUp: After 7 days: "Has it got worse?" Yes → sleep and mood branch (PS1) again.

C-UNCLEAR.title: Could not be classified, general watch
now: Measure pulse, SpO₂, temperature and blood pressure.
Write the complaint into the panel in your own words.
C-UNCLEAR.followUp: After 4–6 hours the panel reopens the tree from the start.
